summary: Reviewed git diff main...HEAD of pr-demo (branch feature/report-export, 1 commit, 5 files, 40 lines added). The change introduces two vulnerabilities: SQL injection in the new report search, and path traversal in the new export download. Two items were excluded: MD5 used for a cache key and a subprocess call with a fixed argument list. One lead is kept as a hypothesis. Pre-existing, not part of this review: /reports trusts the owner parameter. Nothing was executed; exploit scenarios are written from reading the code.

findings.title: SQL injection in search_reports through the owner and q parameters
findings.description: Source: app/server.py:16-17 reads owner and q from the query string. Path: both go unchanged to db.search_reports (app/server.py:18). Sink: app/db.py:14 builds the SQL text with % formatting and app/db.py:15 executes it. Nothing escapes or binds the values, unlike reports_for a few lines above, which uses a placeholder.

proof.poc: Not executed. Request: GET /reports/search?owner=alice&q=x%25'%20UNION%20SELECT%20name,%20sql%20FROM%20sqlite_master%20-- . The q value closes the LIKE string, so the statement becomes ... LIKE '%x%' UNION SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master --%' and the response lists every table and its schema. The same shape reads any table, for any owner.

findings.remediation: Bind the values: conn.execute("SELECT id, title FROM reports WHERE owner = ? AND title LIKE ?", (owner, f"%{term}%")).

findings.title: Path traversal in read_export lets a client read any file the service can read
findings.description: Source: app/server.py:21 reads name from the query string. Path: it goes unchanged to export.read_export (app/server.py:22). Sink: app/export.py:9 joins it to EXPORT_DIR and app/export.py:10 opens the result. os.path.join keeps '..' segments and drops EXPORT_DIR entirely when name is absolute, and the path is never resolved and compared with the export directory.

proof.poc: Not executed. Request: GET /exports?name=../../etc/passwd opens /srv/exports/../../etc/passwd, which is /etc/passwd, and returns it in the response body. GET /exports?name=/etc/passwd does the same, because an absolute second argument replaces the first in os.path.join.

findings.remediation: Resolve and check the prefix: path = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(EXPORT_DIR, name)); reject unless path.startswith(os.path.realpath(EXPORT_DIR) + os.sep). Better: accept an export id and look the file name up server-side.

hypotheses.title: New routes /reports/search and /exports have no authentication check
hypotheses.rationale: The handler adds two routes with no credential check. The existing /reports route has none either, so authentication may be enforced by a proxy or gateway that is not in this repository. The source of trust cannot be read from the diff.
hypotheses.next_step: Ask how /reports is protected in production. If nothing sits in front of the service, PR-002 becomes unauthenticated file read (critical).

artifacts.description: Hunks that add read_export and its route (app/export.py, app/server.py)
